{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that personal moral standards (PMS) would show positive correlations with moral values, virtues, and judgments, and that concern over moral mistakes (CMM) would show distinct relationships with these variables, particularly when controlling for the overlap between the two dimensions.",
  "design": "correlational",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Personal moral standards (PMS) and concern over moral mistakes (CMM) measured via an adapted version of the Frost Multidimensional Perfectionism Scale.",
  "outcome_measure": "Moral values (Adolescents’ Value Scale), virtues (Virtue Adjectives Rating Scale), and moral judgments (forgiveness, gratitude, and wrong behavior judgments).",
  "population_and_setting": "539 university students in the eastern coastal region of the People’s Republic of China.",
  "sample_size_total": 539,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited after classes; no compensation provided.",
  "analysis_plan": "Partial correlations between moral perfectionism dimensions (PMS and CMM) and moral outcomes, controlling for the overlap between PMS and CMM.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "The study used three separate samples (N=168, N=206, N=165) to measure different moral outcomes. The moral perfectionism measure was adapted from the Chinese version of the Frost Multidimensional Perfectionism Scale. Analyses were collapsed across gender after confirming no significant differences in variance-covariance matrices."
}
